neighbours.label: the token ' for' / ' For' (especially introducing a reason or the person something is for)
fire: The general was decorated, and for his service he received a large estate.
She was punished for being late to class three times in a week.
The town is famous for its cheese and its old stone bridge.
My colleagues keep praising the bakery, and for some reason I never go.
He was later honoured for his part in the rescue at sea.
The ancient Greeks had many gods, and for them the sea was sacred.
We bought a small gift for the neighbours who watered our plants.
The workers were fined for parking on the grass outside the office.
quiet: The general was decorated, and after the war he received a large estate.
She was punished because she was late to class three times in a week.
The town is known by its cheese and its old stone bridge.
My colleagues keep praising the bakery, and somehow I never go.
He was later honoured with a medal after the rescue at sea.
The ancient Greeks had many gods, and to them the sea was sacred.
We gave a small gift to the neighbours who watered our plants.
The workers were fined when they parked on the grass outside the office.

notes: Top peaks ' for' x16, ' For' x6, ' After' x3. Near misses replace 'for' with other prepositions/conjunctions.
